agenda: The situation concerning the Democratic Republic of the Congo
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: France's primary objectives are to renew the DRC sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts before their expiry on 1 July 2025, while maintaining Council pressure on the M23 and the RDF following their territorial advances, and reinforcing the integrity of the Luanda and Nairobi processes. The main points of contention during negotiations will be the explicit naming of the Rwanda Defence Forces alongside the M23, which may face caution or demands for balance from some delegations seeking parity with language on the FDLR, and the strengthening of provisions concerning the illicit mineral trade from occupied zones like Rubaya.

messages.Algeria: Algeria fully supports the renewal of the 1533 sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts to curb the violence and illicit exploitation of natural resources in eastern DRC. We insist on highlighting the central role and leadership of the African Union and its Peace and Security Council, alongside the Luanda and Nairobi processes, in line with the principle of African solutions to African problems. We look forward to working with the penholder to reflect these AU-anchored mechanisms in the draft text.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the DRC sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts, and appreciates France's efforts as penholder. We believe the Council should firmly support regional ownership and adhere to the principle of African solutions to African problems, notably through the Luanda and Nairobi frameworks. On the issue of natural resources and sanctions measures, we urge the penholder to adhere strictly to agreed Council language, particularly resolution 2773 (2025) and resolution 1952 (2010), avoiding references to external non-UN standards.
messages.Denmark: Denmark commends France for preparing this well-balanced draft resolution, which rightly addresses the severe escalation, territorial violations, and humanitarian crisis in eastern DRC. We fully support renewing the 1533 sanctions regime and the Group of Experts mandate to ensure monitoring of the arms embargo and illegal mineral exploitation fueling the conflict. Our proposals seek to reinforce accountability for grave violations of international humanitarian law and human rights—particularly conflict-related sexual violence—and to strengthen protections for humanitarian personnel.
messages.Greece: Greece fully supports the timely draft resolution circulated by France to renew the DRC sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts. We strongly endorse the text's reaffirmation of the DRC's sovereignty and territorial integrity, the condemnation of the M23 offensive and external support, and the call to tackle the illicit exploitation of natural resources. We propose a minor addition to PP4 to reaffirm the Security Council's consistent commitment to accountability and the fight against impunity for violations of international humanitarian law.
messages.Guyana: Guyana expresses its appreciation to France for circulating this timely and robust draft text, which builds effectively on resolution 2773 (2025) and addresses the severe escalation in eastern DRC. In close consultation with our African partners (A3+), we believe it is vital to explicitly underscore the primary responsibility of the Congolese State to extend its authority, while highlighting the supportive role of the African Union and regional mechanisms. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder and all Council members towards the prompt, unanimous adoption of this resolution.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan strongly supports the renewal of the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts, in full reaffirmation of the DRC's sovereignty and territorial integrity. As a major troop-contributing country, we emphasize the urgent need to ensure the safety and security of UN peacekeepers and hold perpetrators of attacks against them accountable. Furthermore, to address the root causes of instability, we urge the Council to explicitly address the tracking and disruption of illicit financial flows arising from mineral exploitation.
messages.Panama: Panama commends France for preparing a robust and balanced draft that firmly upholds the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, while renewing the essential sanctions framework and the mandate of the Group of Experts. We fully endorse the demands for the immediate cessation of hostilities, the withdrawal of the M23 and Rwandan forces, and the revitalization of the Luanda and Nairobi processes. Our minor proposed adjustments seek to reinforce our collective commitment to accountability and the protection of vulnerable civilians and humanitarian personnel.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea fully supports the draft resolution circulated by France to renew the DRC sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts. In light of the critical deterioration on the ground and the continued control of major urban centers by M23 with RDF support, it is essential that the Council maintains unity and sends an unequivocal message regarding compliance with resolution 2773 (2025). We strongly endorse the provisions addressing the illicit exploitation of natural resources, the safety and security of MONUSCO peacekeepers, and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the renewal of the 1533 DRC sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts to aid in stabilizing eastern DRC and supporting Congolese sovereignty. However, the Security Council must not impose standards from non-universal organizations such as the OECD, nor should text equate sovereign state armed forces with illegal armed groups. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder to align the draft with previously agreed Council consensus.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone expresses its strong appreciation to France for circulating this timely draft renewing the DRC sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts. In line with our steadfast commitment to African-led solutions and regional peace frameworks, we fully support the core text and believe the Council must maintain firm pressure against all armed groups and external support violating DRC sovereignty. We propose strengthening references to regional mechanisms, particularly the operationalization of the Reinforced Ad-hoc Verification Mechanism under the Luanda process, to ensure effective monitoring of commitments on the ground.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia strongly supports the draft resolution prepared by France, which provides a timely and necessary response to the dramatic escalation in eastern DRC, firmly upholding the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity. We welcome the full renewal of the 1533 sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts, as well as the unequivocal calls for the immediate withdrawal of M23 and RDF forces and the cessation of support to all armed groups, notably the FDLR. We propose two targeted additions to underscore accountability for grave violations, including conflict-related sexual violence and abuses against children, and to reinforce the protection of humanitarian personnel in line with resolution 2730 (2024).
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the timely renewal of the 1533 DRC sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts, which are essential for addressing the illicit resource flows sustaining armed groups. We believe it is vital to strongly anchor Council action in African-led solutions by highlighting the role of the African Union and the Quadripartite framework alongside the Luanda and Nairobi processes. Sustainable peace requires prioritizing regional diplomatic cooperation and dialogue over divisive blame, while firmly upholding the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports France's draft text, which appropriately renews the 1533 sanctions regime and Group of Experts mandate while accurately addressing the unacceptable advances by M23 and the presence of RDF on Congolese territory. Our proposed adjustments seek to reinforce Council resolve by explicitly reiterating that attacks against peacekeepers and humanitarian personnel constitute grounds for sanctions designations, in line with resolution 2773 (2025). We stand ready to work closely with the penholder to ensure swift and unanimous adoption.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks France for its leadership on this draft, which accurately reflects the gravity of the crisis and clearly identifies the destabilizing role of the RDF and M23 in eastern DRC. We strongly support the renewal of the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts, whose reporting remains essential. To ensure accountability and protect peacekeepers and civilians, the Council must explicitly demand the withdrawal of advanced foreign military capabilities, particularly surface-to-air missile systems, and empower the 1533 Sanctions Committee to act without delay on pending and future listing proposals.

steps.summary: Full consensus was reached in Round 2, with all fourteen Council members expressing unreserved support for Revision 1 without any further amendment requests. The draft resolution successfully preserves the Council's unity while upholding DRC sovereignty, extending the 1533 sanctions regime and Group of Experts mandate, and demanding the withdrawal of RDF forces and the cessation of M23 hostilities. The penholder moves the draft resolution directly to a vote, expecting unanimous adoption (15-0-0).

before.France:
France, as the penholder on this file, wishes to thank all members of the Security Council for their constructive engagement throughout the negotiations on this draft resolution.

The renewal of the 1533 sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts on the Democratic Republic of the Congo comes at a critical juncture. The security and humanitarian situation in eastern DRC remains alarming, aggravated by the ongoing offensive of the M23 with the active support of the Rwandan Defence Forces, as well as the actions of other armed groups, notably the FDLR. 

The text before us today reaffirms the clear principles that guide the Council’s action: the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo must be strictly respected; the M23 must cease its hostilities and withdraw from all occupied areas; Rwandan forces must withdraw unconditionally from Congolese territory; and all support to armed groups, including the FDLR, must end immediately. Furthermore, this resolution underscores the necessity of breaking the link between the illegal exploitation and trafficking of natural resources and the financing of armed groups.

The sanctions regime remains a crucial tool to target spoilers of peace, human rights violators, and those who fuel conflict through the illicit trade of Congolese mineral wealth, while the independent reporting of the Group of Experts provides indispensable insight. There is no military solution to this crisis. Only dialogue and the revitalisation of the regional Luanda and Nairobi processes will pave the way toward a lasting peace. 

For all these reasons, France will vote in favour of the draft resolution and calls upon all members of the Council to lend it their unanimous support.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts on the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We would like to thank the French delegation for its efforts in facilitating the consultations that led to this unanimous outcome.

Our vote reflects Algeria’s unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, unity, independence, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as our profound solidarity with the brotherly Congolese people who continue to bear the heavy burden of an agonizing security and humanitarian crisis.

The situation in eastern DRC, particularly across North and South Kivu, remains deeply alarming. The ongoing hostilities, the capture and occupation of key towns and strategic mining areas, and the establishment of parallel administrative structures run contrary to international law and exacerbate the suffering of millions of vulnerable civilians. We reiterate our demand for the M23 to immediately cease all hostilities and unconditionally withdraw from all occupied areas. Furthermore, we reiterate that all external military interference and support to armed groups must cease immediately, and all foreign forces must withdraw from Congolese territory without preconditions. 

At the same time, we stress the necessity of neutralizing all armed groups operating in the region without distinction, including the FDLR, ADF, and local militias, and we urge all parties to strictly uphold international humanitarian law and ensure full, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access.

Mr. President,

Algeria firmly believes that there is no military solution to the crisis in eastern DRC. Lasting peace can only be achieved through genuine political dialogue guided by the principle of African solutions to African problems. In this regard, we reaffirm our full support for the regional peace initiatives led by the African Union, notably the Luanda and Nairobi processes, as well as the quadripartite coordination framework. We encourage all parties to engage in good faith, translate their commitments into concrete actions on the ground, and address the root causes of the conflict, including the illicit exploitation and trafficking of natural resources.

Finally, my delegation pays tribute to the personnel of MONUSCO and the Southern African Development Community Mission in the DRC (SAMIDRC) for their dedication and sacrifices in support of peace and the protection of civilians. Algeria will continue to support all regional and international efforts aimed at restoring enduring peace, stability, and prosperity to the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the entire Great Lakes region.

I thank you.
after.China:
I thank France, as the penholder, for its efforts in preparing and facilitating consultations on this draft resolution.

China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which renews the sanctions measures and the mandate of the Group of Experts on the Democratic Republic of the Congo. China has consistently supported the efforts of the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo to safeguard national sovereignty, territorial integrity, and security, and we support the Security Council in taking necessary and targeted actions to help ease the situation in eastern DRC.

The security and humanitarian situation in eastern DRC remains grave and deeply concerning. Armed conflicts have caused immense civilian casualties and massive displacement, posing a serious threat to regional stability. China urges the M23 and all other armed groups to heed the strong call of the Council, immediately cease all military actions and hostilities, withdraw unconditionally from all illegally occupied areas, and disarm without delay. We also call on all parties concerned to strictly abide by international humanitarian law and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access.

Dialogue and negotiation represent the only viable path to achieving lasting peace and stability in the Great Lakes region. There is no military solution to the conflict in eastern DRC. China consistently supports the principle of seeking African solutions to African problems and firmly backs regional peace initiatives, including the Luanda and Nairobi processes and the quadripartite coordination framework. We encourage the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda to work towards the same goal, rebuild mutual trust, implement their ceasefire commitments, and resolve their differences through friendly consultations.

China has always maintained that Security Council sanctions are a means rather than an end, and that they should always serve the political settlement of relevant issues. The Group of Experts should carry out its work in strict accordance with its mandate, uphold an objective, impartial, and evidence-based approach, and make constructive contributions to the Council’s decision-making. 

China stands ready to continue to work with the international community, regional organizations, and countries in the region to support the Congolese people in achieving lasting peace, stability, and development at an early date.

Thank you, Madam President.
after.Denmark:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Denmark welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution renewing the Democratic Republic of the Congo sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts. We thank France for its leadership and transparent efforts as penholder.

Our vote in favour reflects Denmark’s steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as our conviction that targeted UN sanctions and independent expert reporting are vital tools in countering violence and fostering stability in the Great Lakes region.

The catastrophic escalation of violence and the severe humanitarian crisis in eastern DRC demand our urgent and sustained attention. Millions of civilians continue to endure immense suffering, marked by massive displacement, acute food insecurity, and rampant violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, including conflict-related sexual violence and the horrific recruitment and use of children. There must be full accountability for all such abuses and violations.

The work of the Group of Experts remains indispensable. Their independent and rigorous reporting sheds necessary light on the drivers of instability, not least the illicit trade and exploitation of natural resources, which continues to finance armed actors and prolong the conflict. We urge all Member States and regional stakeholders to cooperate fully with the Group.

Mr. President,

There can be no military solution to this conflict. Denmark reiterates its call on the M23 to immediately cease hostilities, withdraw unconditionally from all occupied areas—including Goma, Bukavu, and Walikale—and end all attempts to establish parallel administrations. Furthermore, foreign military presence without the consent of the DRC government, including the support provided by the Rwanda Defence Forces, must end, and all Rwandan forces must withdraw from Congolese territory without delay. Likewise, all support to armed groups, including the FDLR, must stop immediately.

We urge all parties to respect the ceasefires agreed under regional frameworks and to re-engage in good faith in the Luanda and Nairobi processes. A durable peace can only be achieved through dialogue, regional cooperation, and respect for the UN Charter.

Finally, Denmark reiterates its full support for MONUSCO and commends the peacekeepers and humanitarian workers who continue to operate under exceptionally dangerous conditions to protect vulnerable civilians.

I thank you.
after.Greece:
Mr. President,

Greece welcomed and voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, and we thank the French delegation for its tireless efforts and constructive leadership as penholder on this critical file. 

The unanimous adoption today sends a clear, unified message from the Security Council regarding our collective resolve to address the ongoing conflict in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and to ensure accountability through the renewal of the 1533 sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts.

Greece reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, unity, independence, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as of all States in the region. Respect for international law, the principles of the United Nations Charter, and good-neighbourly relations are paramount and non-negotiable.

We remain profoundly alarmed by the catastrophic security and humanitarian situation in North and South Kivu. The offensive operations of the M23, carried out with the direct support and participation of the Rwandan Defence Forces, along with the seizure of major population centres such as Goma, Bukavu, and Walikale, have caused intolerable suffering and displaced hundreds of thousands of innocent civilians. We reiterate our unequivocal call on the M23 to immediately cease all hostilities and unconditionally withdraw from all occupied areas, and on Rwanda to immediately end its support for the M23 and withdraw all military personnel and assets from Congolese territory. 

Equally, all support to other armed groups, in particular the FDLR, must cease immediately, and all armed groups operating in the region must be demobilized and neutralized without delay. 

Mr. President,

The horrific reports of violations of international humanitarian law and human rights abuses—including summary executions, widespread conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, and the recruitment and use of children—are intolerable. Impunity cannot prevail; all perpetrators must be held to account. We also strongly condemn all attacks against peacekeepers of MONUSCO and SAMIDRC, as well as against humanitarian personnel who operate in extremely perilous conditions. 

Furthermore, we must address the root causes fueling this cycle of violence, including the illicit exploitation and trafficking of natural resources. By holding accountable those who profit from and finance conflict through the illicit mineral trade, the Council's sanctions regime remains an indispensable instrument for peace.

In conclusion, Greece reiterates that there is no military solution to this conflict. We fully support regional diplomatic efforts, notably the Luanda and Nairobi processes, under the auspices of the African Union and regional partners. We urge all parties to honour their commitments, observe a comprehensive and unconditional ceasefire, and return to meaningful dialogue.

I thank you.
after.Guyana:
Guyana welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts on the Democratic Republic of the Congo until 2026. We thank the penholder, France, for its efforts in facilitating this important outcome.

Guyana voted in favour of the resolution in the firm conviction that the 1533 sanctions regime remains an indispensable instrument in countering the illicit proliferation of arms and the illegal exploitation and trade of natural resources, which continue to fuel conflict and instability in the African Great Lakes region. The independent and objective reporting of the Group of Experts is vital to our collective work, and we reiterate our full support for their mandate.

The alarming escalation of violence in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, marked by devastating humanitarian consequences and grave violations of international humanitarian law and human rights, demands decisive and unified action from this Council. We remain deeply concerned by the continued occupation of strategic population centres and mining areas by the M23, enabled by external support. 

Guyana reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. In this regard, we reiterate our call for the M23 to immediately cease hostilities, unconditionally withdraw from Goma, Bukavu, Walikale, and all other captured areas, and halt any attempts to institute parallel administrative structures. We likewise reiterate our call for the Rwanda Defence Forces to cease all support to the M23 and immediately withdraw from Congolese territory. At the same time, we condemn any support provided to the FDLR and other armed groups, and call for the urgent and full implementation of commitments to dismantle and neutralize them.

There can be no military solution to this protracted crisis. Guyana firmly supports regional diplomatic efforts, particularly under the Luanda and Nairobi processes and the quadripartite framework, and we urge all parties to adhere strictly to ceasefire commitments and engage in good faith in dialogue. 

Finally, Guyana commends the dedicated personnel of MONUSCO and SAMIDRC for their service under extremely challenging conditions. We urge all parties to ensure unhindered humanitarian access and to protect civilians, especially women and children, who continue to bear the heaviest burden of this conflict.

I thank you.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the sanctions regime concerning the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the mandate of the Group of Experts. We thank France, as the penholder, for its efforts in guiding this text to a unanimous adoption.

Pakistan remains deeply troubled by the persistent deterioration of the security and humanitarian situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. The ongoing hostilities, displacement of millions of civilians, acute food insecurity, and violations of international humanitarian law demand our continued attention and decisive action. 

Our vote today reflects Pakistan’s consistent and principled commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as our firm adherence to the fundamental principles of the United Nations Charter. Any violation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC is unacceptable and must cease immediately.

We reiterate that there can be no military solution to the conflict in the eastern DRC. The M23 must immediately cease all hostilities and withdraw from all captured areas, including Goma, Bukavu, Walikale, and Rubaya. All foreign forces must withdraw from DRC territory, and all armed groups—including the FDLR, ADF, and local armed groups—must be neutralized and laid down their arms without delay. 

We underline the critical importance of addressing the root causes of the conflict, particularly the illicit exploitation and trafficking of natural resources, which continues to fuel instability and finance armed groups. The renewal of the mandate of the Group of Experts is essential to ensuring transparency, monitoring compliance, and supporting the Council’s efforts in this regard.

Mr. President, as one of the longest-standing and major troop-contributing countries to United Nations peacekeeping operations, including MONUSCO, Pakistan attaches the highest priority to the safety and security of peacekeepers. We pay tribute to the brave men and women of MONUSCO and SAMIDRC who risk their lives daily under perilous conditions. We strongly condemn all attacks against peacekeepers and reiterate that any attempts to impede MONUSCO’s mandate or undermine its security are entirely unacceptable.

Pakistan reaffirms its steadfast support for the regional peace processes, particularly the Luanda and Nairobi processes, under the auspices of the African Union and regional mechanisms. We urge all parties to engage in good faith in dialogue and de-escalation. The international community, and this Council in particular, must remain united and steadfast in helping the people of the Democratic Republic of the Congo achieve lasting peace, stability, and prosperity.

I thank you.
after.Republic of Korea:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The Republic of Korea voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We express our sincere appreciation to France, the penholder, for its dedicated efforts in guiding this Council to another unanimous outcome.

Today’s vote sends a clear and united message: the Security Council remains firmly committed to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. At this critical juncture, when eastern DRC continues to endure immense human suffering and deep instability, council unity is vital.

The 1533 sanctions regime and the Group of Experts remain indispensable tools for promoting peace, accountability, and stability in the region. The illicit exploitation and trafficking of natural resources—including critical minerals—continue to serve as a primary catalyst of violence, enabling armed groups to sustain their destabilizing operations. We fully support the extension of the mandate of the Group of Experts to ensure objective reporting and effective monitoring of the sanctions measures.

My delegation reiterates its profound concern over the continued military escalation. There is no military solution to this conflict. We once again call upon the M23 to immediately cease all hostilities and unconditionally withdraw from all occupied areas, including Goma, Bukavu, and Walikale. We also urge the Rwanda Defence Forces to halt all support to the M23 and immediately withdraw from Congolese territory. Furthermore, the provision of support to other armed groups, notably the FDLR, must cease immediately, and commitments to neutralize them must be fully implemented.

A lasting resolution can only be achieved through peaceful dialogue and regional cooperation. We urge all parties to de-escalate tensions, respect their ceasefire commitments, and re-engage in good faith with the Luanda and Nairobi processes. 

Finally, the Republic of Korea pays tribute to the men and women serving in MONUSCO and SAMIDRC, who operate under increasingly perilous conditions to protect civilians. We reaffirm our steadfast support for their missions and for the people of the Democratic Republic of the Congo in their pursuit of lasting peace and security.

Thank you.
after.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution submitted by France extending the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts on the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Our vote reflects Russia’s consistent and principled position in support of the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as our deep concern over the continuing deterioration of the military, political, and humanitarian situation in the eastern provinces of the country. 

The tragic escalation of recent months, marked by the ongoing offensive of the M23, the capture of major urban centres and strategic areas, and the devastating impact on millions of civilians, demonstrates once again that there can be no military solution to this protracted conflict. We reiterate our call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the full withdrawal of the M23 from all occupied territories, and the cessation of any external military support to armed groups operating in the DRC. At the same time, we stress the necessity of neutralizing all illegal armed formations without distinction, including the FDLR and the ADF.

We remain firmly convinced that a lasting and sustainable peace in the Great Lakes region can be achieved only through political and diplomatic dialogue based on the principle of “African solutions to African problems.” In this regard, we reaffirm our full support for regional mediation efforts, primarily the Luanda and Nairobi processes, and the decisions taken under the auspices of the African Union and subregional organizations. We urge Kinshasa and Kigali to demonstrate political will, strictly adhere to their commitments, and return to constructive negotiations to normalize their relations.

We also underline the importance of addressing the underlying root causes of instability in the eastern DRC, particularly the illicit exploitation and trafficking of natural resources, which continues to fuel armed violence. 

Finally, we emphasize that United Nations sanctions mechanisms are not an end in themselves; they must remain flexible, targeted, and objectively oriented toward facilitating a peaceful settlement and stabilizing the situation on the ground. We expect the Group of Experts to carry out its renewed mandate in strict accordance with the principles of impartiality, objectivity, and transparency, relying on verified and incontrovertible facts.
after.Sierra Leone:
Mr. President,

Sierra Leone welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution renewing the sanctions regime on the Democratic Republic of the Congo and extending the mandate of the Group of Experts established pursuant to resolution 1533 (2004). We commend the delegation of France, as penholder, for its tireless efforts and constructive engagement throughout the negotiation process to achieve consensus on this important text.

Sierra Leone voted in favour of this resolution in accordance with our principled foreign policy and unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Our vote also reflects our firm belief in African-led solutions to African challenges, anchored in the principles of the Charter of the United Nations and regional cooperation.

The Council’s unanimous decision today comes against the backdrop of an extraordinarily grave and deteriorating security and humanitarian situation in eastern DRC. The continued offensive by the M23, their control of strategic urban centers and vital economic hubs, including Goma, Bukavu, and the Rubaya mining district, and the direct involvement of foreign forces represent a direct threat to regional peace and security and an unacceptable violation of the territorial integrity of the DRC. 

We reiterate our strong demand that the M23 immediately cease all hostilities, halt its offensive, dismantle parallel administrative structures, and fully and unconditionally withdraw from all occupied areas. Furthermore, foreign forces must withdraw without delay from the territory of the DRC, and all external support to armed groups, notably the M23, must cease immediately. At the same time, we condemn any support provided to the FDLR and other armed groups and reiterate the imperative of neutralizing these negative forces in line with regional commitments.

Sierra Leone remains convinced that there is no military solution to the crisis in eastern DRC. Sustainable peace can only be achieved through genuine political dialogue. In this regard, we reaffirm our full support for the revitalized Luanda and Nairobi processes, led respectively by President João Lourenço and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, as well as the AU Quadripartite framework and the diplomatic efforts undertaken in Doha. We urge all parties to honor their commitments, implement an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, and return to good-faith negotiations.

The illicit exploitation and illicit trade of natural resources, including coltan and gold, remain a central driver of instability, financing the proliferation of weapons and empowering illegal armed actors. The sanctions regime and the work of the Group of Experts are vital instruments to enhance transparency, disrupt illicit financial and supply networks, and ensure accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and human rights abuses, including sexual and gender-based violence and the recruitment of children.

Finally, we express our profound concern over the humanitarian catastrophe in North and South Kivu, marked by massive displacement and severe protection challenges. We urge all parties to facilitate full, safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access to all civilians in need, and we reiterate our support for MONUSCO and regional peace efforts, paying tribute to all peacekeepers who have made the ultimate sacrifice in the service of peace.

Sierra Leone will continue to work closely with Council members, regional partners, and the Congolese authorities to support the path toward lasting peace, stability, and development in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the wider African Great Lakes region.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Slovenia:
Mr. President,

Slovenia voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which extends the sanctions regime and renews the mandate of the Group of Experts on the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We thank France, as the penholder, for its efforts in steering the negotiations toward a unanimous outcome.

Today’s vote sends a necessary and united signal from this Council at a time of grave crisis in eastern DRC. The continued military offensive by the M23, supported by the Rwanda Defence Forces, and their control over major population centres, including Goma and Bukavu, have deepened an already catastrophic humanitarian disaster and caused immense suffering for millions of civilians.

Slovenia reiterates its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Any violation of its territorial integrity is unacceptable. We call on the M23 to immediately halt all hostilities, dismantle its parallel administration, and withdraw unconditionally from all occupied areas. Furthermore, we reiterate our call on Rwanda to cease all support for the M23 and immediately withdraw its troops and military assets from Congolese territory. At the same time, we condemn any support provided to the FDLR and call for its complete and immediate neutralization.

Mr. President,

The human toll of this conflict is appalling. Slovenia remains profoundly concerned by widespread violations of international humanitarian law and serious human rights abuses, including summary executions, sexual and gender-based violence, and the recruitment and use of children by armed groups. Perpetrators of these heinous crimes must be held accountable. There can be no impunity for violations of international law.

We also underline the urgent need to address the link between the conflict and the illicit exploitation and trade of natural resources, which fuels the violence and enriches armed groups and illicit networks. In this regard, the targeted sanctions regime and the independent reporting of the Group of Experts remain indispensable instruments for the Council to promote accountability and deter further destabilization.

Finally, we reiterate that there is no military solution to this conflict. We urge all parties to de-escalate, adhere strictly to a ceasefire, and engage in good faith in regional diplomatic tracks, particularly the Luanda and Nairobi processes. 

Thank you.
after.Somalia:
Somalia voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, renewing the sanctions regime on the Democratic Republic of the Congo and extending the mandate of the Group of Experts.

My delegation remains deeply troubled by the continued escalation of violence and the severe humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. The massive displacement of civilians, the high levels of human suffering, and the violations of international humanitarian law and human rights demand our collective and urgent attention. 

Somalia reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We reiterate that any violation of the DRC's sovereignty is unacceptable and that there can be no military solution to this conflict.

We renew our call for an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, the cessation of hostilities by all armed groups—including the M23, the FDLR, and the ADF—and the immediate withdrawal of all foreign forces and armed groups from the territory of the DRC. Furthermore, addressing the illicit exploitation and illicit trade of natural resources, which continues to fuel the cycle of conflict and arms proliferation in the region, remains vital.

As an African member of this Council, Somalia firmly believes that lasting peace can only be achieved through constructive dialogue, good-neighbourliness, and regional cooperation, anchored in the principle of African solutions to African problems. We commend the continued diplomatic initiatives undertaken under the auspices of the African Union, particularly the Luanda and Nairobi processes, and the quadripartite framework. We urge all parties to engage in good faith in these regional peace tracks and fully implement their commitments.

It is our hope that the targeted measures renewed today and the impartial reporting of the Group of Experts will contribute constructively to halting the flow of weapons to armed groups, protecting civilians, and supporting the regional diplomatic efforts aimed at achieving lasting peace and stability in the Great Lakes region.

I thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution renewing the Democratic Republic of the Congo sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts, and we thank France for its leadership as penholder.

The ongoing crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo is causing catastrophic humanitarian suffering and severe violations of international humanitarian law and human rights. Today’s adoption reaffirms the Security Council’s continued resolve to address the drivers of instability and conflict in the Great Lakes region.

The United Kingdom’s position remains unequivocal. There can be no military solution to this conflict. We reaffirm our unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. 

M23 must immediately cease hostilities, halt its offensive, and withdraw unconditionally from all captured territory, including Goma, Bukavu, and the Rubaya mining area. We reiterate our call on Rwanda to end all support to M23 and withdraw the Rwanda Defence Forces and its military assets from Congolese territory without delay. Equally, any support provided by the Congolese armed forces or any other actor to armed groups, notably the FDLR, is completely unacceptable and must stop, and commitments to neutralize the FDLR must be swiftly implemented.

The illicit exploitation and trade of natural resources continue to fuel armed groups and perpetuate violence against civilians. The work of the Group of Experts is vital to shedding light on these illicit networks, arms trafficking, and sanctions violations, and all parties must cooperate fully with their mandate.

Finally, we urge all parties to de-escalate, adhere to a comprehensive ceasefire, and return in good faith to the regional diplomatic processes, particularly the Luanda and Nairobi frameworks. Sustainable peace will only be achieved through political dialogue and genuine regional cooperation.
after.United States of America:
The United States welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution, renewing the DRC sanctions regime and the mandate of the Group of Experts. We thank France for its leadership as penholder.

The work of the Group of Experts is vital to our collective efforts to understand the drivers of conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and to hold those responsible for fueling violence accountable. Their independent, fact-based reporting provides this Council and the international community with the transparency required to take informed and decisive action.

The humanitarian and security crisis in eastern DRC has reached catastrophic levels. The ongoing offensive by the M23, enabled and directly supported by the Rwanda Defence Forces, has brought immense suffering to millions of civilians, forced massive displacement, and triggered egregious human rights abuses, including conflict-related sexual violence and the recruitment of children. 

The Security Council has made its expectations clear, both today and in resolution 2773: M23 must immediately cease hostilities, halt its advance, and withdraw completely and unconditionally from all captured territory, including Goma, Bukavu, Walikale, and the Rubaya mining district. Furthermore, Rwanda must immediately cease all support to M23 and withdraw all RDF personnel and military equipment, including sophisticated surface-to-air missile systems, from Congolese territory. 

We also reiterate our call for an end to all support provided by Congolese armed forces to armed groups, notably the FDLR. The DRC must fulfill its commitments to neutralize the FDLR, an armed group responsible for horrific atrocities and a persistent source of regional instability.

Additionally, this Council cannot ignore the illicit exploitation and illicit trade of critical minerals, such as coltan and gold, which directly finance armed groups and perpetuate the cycle of violence. We urge all Member States and industry stakeholders to ensure full transparency and traceability in their supply chains.

The United States has consistently demonstrated its commitment to accountability, including through our own targeted sanctions against individuals who fuel this conflict and undermine regional stability. We once again urge the 1533 Sanctions Committee to act without delay to designate those responsible for prolonging the violence and violating international humanitarian law.

There is no military solution to this conflict. We reaffirm our strong support for African-led mediation efforts, including the Luanda and Nairobi processes, and we urge all parties to honor their ceasefire commitments and return to diplomatic dialogue in good faith. 

Thank you, Mr. President.
